description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of media sources cited or referenced in a political discourse analysis, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet and its proportional contribution to the overall dataset. The chart is divided into 15 distinct segments, each labeled with the name of a media entity. The largest segment, colored blue, corresponds to “Breitbart” and accounts for 14% of the total. The second largest, gray, is labeled “Other” and represents 13%. Following these are “Drudge Report” and “The Daily Caller,” each occupying 8% and colored orange and green respectively. “Fox News” and “CNN” each account for 3%, appearing as small red and purple segments respectively. “The Huffington Post” and “NPR” each represent 7% and are colored red and purple respectively. “Vox” and “The Guardian” each account for 6% and are shown in brown and pink respectively. “BBC” and “RT” each represent 5% and are colored gray and yellow respectively. “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Daily Mail,” “Red State,” and “Shareblue” each represent 3% and are depicted in various shades of blue, green, and purple. The chart includes percentage labels within each slice, and while the segments are arranged in descending order of size from the top right, there is no explicit legend provided. No slices are visually emphasized beyond their proportional size and color coding.
